facts.value: The Student Secretariat is your point of contact regarding the management of your student status.

Services include application, issuance of the Goethe Card (student ID), semester dates, semester fee and re-registration, change of subject, dual study, leave of absence, exmatriculation and refund of fees.
Many issues can be handled conveniently by post or online.
Detailed information for international students studying in Frankfurt can be found on the Global Office's pages.
Topics include residence rights, working while studying, and questions about work permits.
Online portals allow for self-management of personal data and electronic management of student and examination data.
Comprehensive support offers are available for students with disabilities or chronic illnesses to ensure a barrier-free study.
There are offers for students who feel overwhelmed, anxious about exams or are otherwise struggling.
The university and the student union offer numerous advisory and support services on the topic of studying with children.
Pregnant students should consult the examination office regarding the new regulations on maternity protection at the beginning of their pregnancy.
The university provides various advisory and support services concerning discrimination and equality.
The Goethe-Uni Law Clinic offers free legal advice for issues related to residence, migration and social law, and applications for social benefits.
The association 'Mieter helfen Mietern e.V.' provides rental law advice for students of Goethe University.
